thread.title: AT&T, Verizon Under Scrutiny For Hindering Carrier-Switching Technology

author: REINHARDT KRAUSE
title: AT&T, Verizon Under Scrutiny For Hindering Carrier-Switching Technology
text:
The U.S. Department of Justice is probing whether Verizon Communications ( VZ ), AT&T ( T ) and a wireless industry group hindered a technology that makes it easier for consumers to switch service providers, a report said Friday.
X The DOJ has asked AT&T, Verizon and the GSMA, a mobile industry standards-setting group, for information related to the investigation, reported the New York Times .
The probe into possible collusion between AT&T and Verizon to delay usage of the technology known as electronic-SIM or "e-SIM" in smartphones reportedly began five months ago. The software technology lets people switch mobile-phone providers without having to insert a new SIM card into their handset.
Apple Has Used E-SIM technology uses reprogrammable software to provide access to networks operated by Verizon, AT&T, T-Mobile US ( TMUS ) or Sprint ( S ). While Apple ( AAPL ) has dabbled with the technology in its devices, its adoption has been slower than expected in smartphones.

Please contact customer service CLOSE Apple last year sold a version of the iPhone X at its website that used e-SIM technology. The cellular-enabled version of the Apple Watch also uses similar software.
Apple has forged ahead cautiously with e-SIM technology, aiming not to damage relations with its distribution partners. Samsung also has used e-SIM technology in a few products.
Some market researchers had forecast that most smartphone makers would build e-SIM technology into devices by 2018 or 2019 but adoption has been slower than expected.
Shares in AT&T fell 0.4% to 34.67 on the stock market today . Verizon was down 1% to 47.90.
